[AMD] Support controlling WGP/CU mode for RDNA (#11910)

On gfx10+ a work-group is by default spread across both CUs of a work-group
processor (WGP mode). CU mode confines it to a single CU, which changes
what a work-group shares  one vector L0 cache rather than two.

LLVM exposes this as the `+cumode` subtarget feature, but Triton passes
an empty feature string in `make_amdgcn`, so every RDNA kernel is compiled for
WGP mode with no supported way to ask for the alternative.

This PR adds the option. It is **off by default**, so no existing kernel
changes behaviour.

[GSan] Support graphs of kernel dependencies (#12023)

GSan currently derives inter-kernel ordering from stream launch order,
which cannot represent branches and joins in explicit CUDA graphs.
Replace the implicit predecessor selection with per-node launch
descriptors: full dependencies acquire completion clocks at kernel
entry, while programmatic dependencies acquire them at `gdc_wait`.

Add graph boundary helpers, replay and lifetime handling, and immutable
completion snapshots for dependencies established by CUDA events. Eager
launches use the same descriptor interface. Tests cover fork/join
graphs, PDL, repeated launches, stream transitions, lifetime cleanup,
and detection of unordered accesses and missing waits. Stream capture
remains unsupported.

### Validation

- Rebuilt the PR source on GB300 and verified the patched test checksum.
GSan suite: **421 passed, 2 xfailed** in the main phase; **8 passed, 1
skipped** in the multi-GPU phase. The multi-GPU phase passed on retry
after a TCP port collision during process-group setup.
- Repeated both graph PDL failure cases 50 times each across eight
workers: **100 passed**. These retain exact diagnostic and
source-location assertions.
- All commit hooks passed, including Ruff, YAPF, mypy, and Python syntax
checks; `git diff --check` passed.

[AMD] Emit packed scaled_upcast layout for dot decomposition (#11909)

`amdgpu.scaled_upcast` requires a layout which has `groupSize` (min 4)
elements along `axis` held by a thread. When doing software emulation
for scaled_dot we currently emit a blocked layout invalidating this
requirement and rely on RemoveLayoutConversation to fix this for us.
With https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11760 this no longer
reliably works and this PR emits an legal packed initial layout. We also
treat it as a layout anchor to avoid invalidating the layouts with
RemoveLayoutConversions.

This also allows us to have a proper verifier to ensure the layouts are
compatible and we no longer trigger late asserts when lowering to llvm.
The other option would be to implement a software path were we lower via
unpacked instructions, but it would silently regress performance if we
mess up the layouts, especially in Gluon.

## Known issues
This will break if the axis dimension is too small so we do not have
enough unique elements along `axis`. This is a latent bug and would
trigger an assert in the lowering before this PR (it's now a verifier
fail). This will be fixed in a follow up PR.

[Gluon][NVIDIA] Support L2 cache policies on TMA transfers (#12000)

Gluon TMA operations currently cannot express L2 eviction hints, and
descriptor-load rewrites discard their cache policy. Add the single
`cache_policy` argument to `async_load`, `async_load_im2col`,
`async_store`, `async_gather`, and `async_scatter`, including the
Blackwell reexports.

All five APIs accept the existing generic or NVIDIA `CachePolicy`
objects, including `CachePolicy(l2=FractionalEvictionPolicy(...))`.
Omission or `None` emits no hint; explicit detailed `evict_normal`
remains a real L2 policy. There is no separate `eviction_policy`
argument on the TMA frontend. Share the L2-only validation across the
Python APIs and TMA IR operations: reject L1 policies, cache modifiers,
and prefetch sizes, while retaining the existing volatile-load
rejection.

Use one optional `cachePolicy` IR attribute and the common
decoder/policy generator. Emit the 64-bit policy operand on every
message, after im2col offsets and the multicast mask where present. Keep
existing no-policy C++ builder overloads. Forward load policies through
descriptor lowering, pipelining, NVWS, and Hopper warp specialization;
preserve gather/scatter policies through layout conversion. Memory
effects, fences, barriers, and completion accounting are unchanged.

The obsolete TMA-load textual `cacheModifier`/`evictionPolicy` syntax is
replaced by `cachePolicy`; generic IR with legacy `cache`/`evict`
attributes diagnoses instead of silently dropping them.

### Validation

Compiler and GPU validation at 3b0560557d, before the Python-only
removal of the separate `eviction_policy` argument:

- Full lit suite: 302 passed, 2 unsupported.
- Full Gluon frontend suite: 725 passed, 199 skipped.
- Focused frontend/assembler tests: 193 passed, 15 unsupported
architecture cases skipped. Covers SM90 loads/stores and SM100
gather/scatter through pinned PTXAS 12.9.86 / 13.4.59.
- Focused GPU tests: 175 passed, covering rank 1/2/5,
default/generic/NVIDIA policies, false predicates, im2col, multicast,
and multi-CTA gather/store/scatter.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed.

The subsequent Python-only API cleanup passed pre-commit and
signature/call-site checks. The existing tests now pass policies through
`cache_policy`; GPU tests were not rerun for that cleanup, and the
compiler was not rebuilt.

The load implementation at d880253fcc also passed the upstream H100 and
GB200 jobs. Those jobs will rerun for this extension.

Performance qualification at d880253fcc: a same-address hot/cold TMA
microbenchmark passed exact copy/reduction checks. Across two runs,
typed `evict_first` changed approximately 55.4 us to 51.8 us and 73.7 us
to 70.3 us in its two configurations; identical-kernel controls differed
by up to 1.4%. A separate 16-GB300 integration workload measured +4.95%
and +4.94% latency when only TMA hints were removed (+4.94% combined),
against +0.024% for the identical-kernel control. All 96 TMA-specific
distributed correctness checks passed. These observations are
workload-specific and do not establish performance gains for
gather/store/scatter. The model and ablation instrumentation are
excluded from this PR.

[BACKEND] Minimise bank conflicts when lowering {ld,st}matrix.trans (#12033)

`{ld,st}matrix.trans` has a peculiar shape, in that the registers
we choose affect the 8 groups (the 8 rows in the `{ld,st}matrix` tile
of 4 banks that are moved in each transaction. In this PR we choose the
registers so that they minimise (in this order):
- The number of bank conflicts
- Two heuristics to reduce PRMTs

Closes https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/11927
